R7 — icon artwork fidelity (original Figma export vs normalised library asset)

For a deterministic sample of variants:

  • every category;
  • both styles;
  • all five sizes;
  • every per-size file;
  • every 25th variant.
The fixture rasterises the original category export (src/icons/originals/…), cropped to the variant's Figma box, and the normalised asset at the same pixel size. The original is cropped as a vector (its own viewBox re-pointed at the box). Both are drawn on white at 2× the icon's true pixel size. The scaled-down exports (Figma's 4,096 px cap) are therefore re-rasterised from their vectors, not compared at their tiny exported size. The fixture compares the ink masks (pixels darker than mid-grey), so colour normalisation does not matter. A variant passes when at most 2% of pixels disagree and the ink area differs by at most 3%. That tolerance covers antialiasing at shape edges; a wrong or shifted shape fails.
